error_codes.description: HTTP status codes this row matches. Example: [429, 503].

words.description: Case-insensitive substrings of the error message. Example: ["rate limit", "overloaded"].

words_match.description: "any" matches when one word is present; "all" requires every word. Defaults to "any".

when.description: Trigger clause. Supplying both kinds matches when either the code or the word clause matches.

smart_overrides.description: Per-error overrides of the values above, applied in declaration order with later explicit values winning. Not a separate budget: a matching row replaces which values the retry counter uses. A configured array replaces the shipped rows entirely.

retry.description: Retries for errors where the provider returned nothing — network failures, 5xx, stream death, rate limits. The request is resent unchanged; no context intervention is attempted.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

enabled.description: Master switch for every compaction feature. When false, ppie-recover reads no other value in this object: it initiates no compaction, waits for none, and warns about none. Compaction is left entirely to Pi. Containment is positional and admits no exception — a nested value is governed by this switch whether it causes an action or is purely advisory. Nested values are retained, so re-enabling restores the configured behavior. The sibling prune group has its own enabled gate and is not governed by this switch.
Allow preventive compaction before an overflow occurs.

at_context_ratio.description: Fraction of the model context window that triggers preventive compaction. Not an on/off switch: the value is retained while enabled is false. Evaluated at Pi's agent_settled checkpoint, so a continuous tool-use loop crossing the ratio is left running.

dynamic.description: Preventive compaction at a context threshold. Independent of forced compaction; neither implies the other.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

enabled.description: Allow ppie-recover to force a compaction when Pi has not resolved an overflow itself.

wait_seconds_before_first_attempt.description: Delay before forcing the first compaction, independent of the retry schedule. If Pi core or another compaction extension starts one during this window, ppie-recover cancels its own and defers to that compaction without consuming an attempt.

max_attempts.description: Forced compactions before recovery falls through to pruning. Own counter, independent of retry.max_attempts. One attempt is consumed per compaction that did not resolve the overflow — whether it failed mid-flight, reported nothing to compact, or completed without freeing enough. Minimum 1; use enabled to switch forced compaction off.

warn_after_seconds.description: Advisory warning when a compaction has not finished. 0 disables. Never alters recovery state.

give_up_after_no_progress_seconds.description: First observation window of the two-stage abandonment check: compaction lifecycle state is snapshotted, then compared after this delay. 0 disables the watchdog.

give_up_confirm_seconds.description: Second observation window, entered only when the first found no change. Two consecutive unchanged observations release compaction ownership; abandoning never infers that the compaction completed.

forced.description: Compaction ppie-recover initiates itself after an overflow error that Pi has not resolved.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

compaction.description: Every compaction concern ppie-recover owns. Pi's native reserveTokens and keepRecentTokens are never altered.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

enabled.description: Allow pruning after the forced-compaction budget is spent. Destructive; off by default.

max_attempts.description: Prune attempts before recovery stops. Own counter, independent of retry.max_attempts. Default 1: the removal target is calculated from the provider's reported overage plus reserve and margin, so a correct calculation clears the limit on the first attempt. A second attempt means the calculation was wrong, not that more removal was needed.

removal_fractions.description: Escalation ladder: the fraction of eligible content removed on each successive attempt. Unique and strictly increasing. Only the first entry is reached while max_attempts is 1.

target_priorities.description: Higher priority is removed first; ties are removed oldest first.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

tool_priorities.description: Removal order for named tool results within tool_results. Unlisted tools are ordered by age. Example: { "bash": 5, "read": 4 } removes bash output before read output.

^_.description: Documentation metadata ignored by ppie-recover at runtime.

block_markers.description: Substrings identifying marked blocks, governed by target_priorities.marked_blocks.

extra_overage_tokens.description: Headroom removed beyond the provider's measured overage, absorbing token-estimate error.

prune.description: Last resort after the forced-compaction budget is spent — or immediately when compaction is disabled. Unstable interface — it may change or be removed in a future version. Trims the outgoing provider payload only; session history is never rewritten, and prompts, skills, system instructions, and user messages are never eligible. Once recovery enters pruning it never returns to compaction.
